block-handbooktext-brickcourse-*:
Bricks can be fired in a pit kiln, which will give a limited set of colors. They can also be fired in a beehive kiln, which will allow a much greater range of colors to be made. Furthermore, the larger format bricks of 4 courses per block, can be crafted to a smaller size that has double the courses.

Polychromy

different colors of bricks can be combined via chiseling, and 3 basic patterns can be made - running, soldier, and header bonds. Each of these bonds can also be switched to an offset variant, and running bonds have an additional two variants (1/4 offset and 3/4 offset). Via the use of these three basic patterns and their offsets, virtually any pattern of brickwork can be made. Research 'brick polychromy' to learn more.

blockdesc-bomb-scrap: This bomb is particularly effective for damaging creatures, but completely inneffective against stone or ore.

item-handbooktext-cassava:
Cassava is a useful vegetable, it can be added as a starchy vegetable to meals, or dried and ground to make flour. The Cassava plant tolerates most warm climates and yields a good quantity of the crop.

Raw cassava is toxic, however. To make it safe to eat, it must first be soaked in water for a day (hint: use a barrel). The Soaked cassava must be peeled with a knife. Cassava can then be added to meals as a vegetable. Once peeled, it must be used within a few hours or else it will start to dry out. When dried its only use is to be ground to make Cassava flour.
itemdesc-burnedbrick-clinker: Clinkers are bricks that have been over-cooked, their surfaces vitrified like glass, and are not very good for building. One must use more of them to get a neat result.
itemdesc-clay-*: Can be formed into basic pottery items. <hk>shift</hk> + <hk>rightmouse</hk> click on the ground to begin clay forming.
block-handbooktext-rawclay-red: Red clay can be found anywhere there is soil, and a minimum level of rainfall. It can occur at any elevation. It will be more plentiful when soil layers are thick. It does not occur in sand or gravel, nor in extreme cold regions.
block-handbooktext-rawclay-blue: Blue clay can be found at low elevations anywhere there is soil, and a minimum level of rainfall. It will be more plentiful when soil layers are thick. It does not occur in sand or gravel, nor in extreme cold regions, and also does not occur very far above sea level.
item-handbooktext-clay-fire:
Fire clay is found naturally in areas of bauxite sand or gravel in small patches at the surface, and underlaying black and anthracite coal deposits in large patches, underground. It can also be crafted by combining red or blue clay with powdered flint.

Special Uses
Fireclay is also useful in tempering and quenching. Place a piece of fireclay in the crafting grid alongside a tool or weapon head that does not have a handle. This will cover it in a thin layer of clay, which will improve durability of the finished item during quenching.
item-handbooktext-clay-blue*: Blue clay is found as surface deposits in any area with high enough preciptation (so not deserts) and high enough temperature (so not the arctic). It is only found at low elevations, near sea level.
item-handbooktext-clay-red*: Red clay is found as surface deposits in any area with high enough preciptation (so not deserts) and high enough temperature (so not the arctic). It can be found at any elevation above sea level.
item-handbooktext-clearquartz: Smelting quartz requires temperatures too high for regular fuels. Use a bloomery to smelt quartz into glass.
itemdesc-flaxfibers: 4 of them can be turned into twine
item-handbooktext-flaxtwine: Twine can be used to repair damaged clothing by 10%. Holding the twine with your mouse pointer, <hk>leftmouse</hk> click on the piece of clothing or armor to be repaired, in your Character inventory.
itemdesc-corruptflint: Can be knapped into incredibly durable stone tools and weapons. <hk>shift</hk> + <hk>rightmouse</hk> click on the ground to begin knapping (a second stone is also needed).
item-handbooktext-ingot-blistersteel: Blister steel is obtained via the steel making process, and must be refined on an anvil to turn it into steel.
item-handbooktext-ingot-steel: Steel is obtained via the steel making process.
item-handbooktext-corruptore-lapislazuli: Items that are a pigment can be used to write on signs, and sometimes also to dye cloth.
item-handbooktext-ore-quartz: Smelting quartz requires temperatures too high for regular fuels. Use a bloomery to smelt quartz into glass.
item-handbooktext-ore-alum: Alum is a deposit that occurs only in sedimentary stone (except bauxite), as a result of the evaporation of lakes in hot climates. One will generally need to travel to a southern desert to find these deposits. They will always be found atop the highest stone layer, but below non-stone layers such as dirt, gravel, or sand. It is possible for it to leave nuggets atop these layers however, in the same way as other surface ores.
itemdesc-powderedsulfur: Used for bombs and bandages. Smells bad.
item-handbooktext-rawbrick-blue: Raw blue bricks will always be the same color when fired in a pit kiln, however, when fired in a beehive kiln, other colors can be obtained. See beehive kiln entry for details.
item-handbooktext-rawbrick-red: Raw red bricks will always be the same color when fired in a pit kiln, however, when fired in a beehive kiln, other colors can be obtained. See beehive kiln entry for details.
item-handbooktext-rawbrick-fire: Unlike blue and red bricks, fireclay bricks will always be the same color when fired, whether in a pit kiln, or a beehive kiln.

Time to make some bombs!

...or a fertile garden!

itemdesc-ore-emerald: Looks like a piece of colored glass? I wonder what is it good for.
itemdesc-seeds-pumpkin: When planting, make sure to leave a lot of extra space around it
item-handbooktext-stick: Sticks have a chance to drop from normal leaf blocks, and are guaranteed to drop from branchy leaves. You can also find them laying on the ground in forests. If you fell an entire tree with an axe, leaves will also break, however, you'll get far fewer sticks than if you had broken the leaf blocks individually first. The drop chance from breaking leaf blocks is not affected by the type of tool used to break the block: but you can use shears to harvest sticks swiftly.
item-handbooktext-bowstave-*-raw: Bowstaves are typically left on a tool rack to dry, though they can also dry in inventory. Containers will inhibit drying.
item-handbooktext-saw-*: Using a saw to break tree trunk blocks will allow you to obtain individual blocks without altering the rest of the tree, unlike an axe.
item-handbooktext-shears-*: Shears will break all leaf (and branchy leaf) blocks in a 3x3x3 cube centered on the block they are used on. Thus they can be used to harvest sticks, and potentially tree seeds, very fast.
itemdesc-blade-longsword-admin: With great power comes great responsibility.
itemdesc-blade-falx-*: A specialized weapon for fighting the unnatural. The creatures hide metal in their flesh and their blood flows like sludge. A simple sword will not do here.
itemdesc-blade-scrap-scrap: Made from a scrap weapon kit. “Materials are hard to come by these days. Work with what you've got.”
itemdesc-blade-blackguard-iron: Short and lightweight. Made for skirmishes in the narrow tunnels.
itemdesc-blade-forlorn-iron: An elegant blade; it was of little use against what was coming for them.
itemdesc-spear-generic-hacking: Attack a locust for a chance to convert it into an ally. It will follow and protect you, but you can only maintain one converted locust at a time. Bring the wayward children home.
itemdesc-*-scrap: Made from a scrap weapon kit. “Materials are hard to come by these days. Work with what you've got.”
item-handbooktext-axe-*: Most tools and weapons can be leaned against a wall using <hk>ctrl</hk> + <hk>shift</hk> + <hk>rightmouse</hk>-click (up to two per wall block)
block-handbooktext-torch-extinct-up: When placed, an extinguished torch can be relit using a firestarter or a torch.
handbook-charcoal-drawing:
Charcoal can be used to write labels on chests: shift rightmouse-click on the label to write.

Charcoal can be used to draw symbols and cave paintings on hard surfaces. While aiming at a hard surface, use toolmodeselect key (Tool Mode) to change symbol. ctrl-rightmouse-click to draw. Chalk, hematite and limonite can also be used for different color effects.

Chalk can be used to write labels on chests: shift rightmouse-click on the label to write.

Chalk can be used to draw symbols and cave paintings on hard surfaces. While aiming at a hard surface, use toolmodeselect key (Tool Mode) to change symbol. ctrl-rightmouse-click to draw. Charcoal, hematite and limonite can also be used for different color effects.
handbook-limonite-drawing: Rich pieces of Limonite can be used to draw symbols and cave paintings on hard surfaces. item-handbooktext-creature-chicken-*:
Chickens are fed using a small trough, and will lay eggs in a hen box (or on the ground if no henbox is available). Chickens must be well fed to lay. Chickens must also be well fed to sit in the henbox for long enough to hatch the eggs.

A rooster is necessary, for fertile eggs.
itemdesc-creature-sheep-bighorn-*: These sheep are found in temperate climates, at higher elevations
itemdesc-creature-sheep-mouflon-*: These sheep are found in temperate climates, at lower elevations
blockdesc-corruptmushroom-*:
Mushroom
Use knife to harvest quicker
block-handbooktext-corruptmushroom-*: Mushrooms grow in a variety of areas, though forests are the most common place to find them. Once harvested, the mushrooms will not reappear until certain conditions are met, such as time passed, or rainfall. They will reappear in the vinicity of the original patch, but not exactly the same spot.

item-handbooktext-wormgrunter: A worm grunting stick is used in conjunction with a stick in your offhand.  Hold <hk>shift</hk> + <hk>rightmouse</hk> on a patch of bare soil.  The sound the of the stick being run along the ridges of the grunter makes vibrations that are - to a worm - similar to a mole, scaring them to the surface.  Not every block of dirt will have worms, and the wetter the climate, the better the chance. Cold weather will result in fewer worms, and when it is freezing they will not respond at all.
